full_page.content:
1947, May 25.
Doctor J. P. Young
Page 4.
Going back to your family, however, is a secondary matter and can in a number of ways be bridged over without great difficulties. If ever again you get back into the grace of God by a good, humble confession, that "preternatural fear and dislike you now experience for things you once revered and loved, will at once weaken, and, little by little you will in all probability come to your old happy self again.
But to dance along the "wide road that leads to destruction" and in a state of most probable mortal sin, dily-dallying with a possibility of some day obtaining the grace of God and eternal salvation, is a fearfully perilous course to take. To my mind it is positively following the steps of our unfortunate judge above referred to, in an appallingly close imitation, and something to checkup on at every and all costs.
Hoping dear Doctor, that I have not been over harsh in my conclusions and that this may not discourage you. Rather on the contrary that it may simply wake you up before it's too late, from your most threatening drowsyness, I beg to remain
Sincerely at your service in any way wherein I may be able to do you a favor.
Tr. Solanus, O.F.M. Cap.
Please do not forget Doctor; I need prayers as well as any other poor sinner. In this it seems to me we are all in like need -- not knowing, as the great Apostal of the Gentiles teaches: "not knowing if we be worthy of love or punishment, - love or hatred."
